closeness_check fires ClosenessViolation as soon as a cell's box is at certified distance > eps from the whole other curve (at any width, not only at the width floor); the floor-gated check alone would bisect the entire displaced tail of the trimmed fixture (~2^45 cells) and exhaust the budget as ClosenessUnresolved

packet test 3 cites the BG-FID-008 witness verbatim (R + eps*cos(t/2)); its maximum deviation is exactly eps, and Decision 2(i) requires every cell to pair with sup_distance <= eps, which the seam cell at radius R+eps cannot satisfy (sup-distance > eps to every circle cell), so (i) returns ClosenessUnresolved instead of passing; the test therefore uses amplitude eps/2 so (i) certifies while the fibre stays 2-to-1

the packet's 'parameter gap qualifies' is ambiguous; I implement it as the cell pair CONTAINING a qualifying parameter pair (max parameter gap >= arc_gap). The min-gap reading makes the packet's own test numbers unreachable: for the circle at arc_gap = pi (the attainable maximum wrapped gap) no non-degenerate cell pair has min wrapped gap >= pi, and for the ellipse the wrap-side minimizer's cells have min wrapped gap < 2, so both helpers would return +inf, contradicting test 1 (~4) and test 12 (~0.84). Under the max-gap reading the certificate is a sound lower bound: the cell pair containing the true minimizer always qualifies and its box-to-box distance is <= the true value
